{"reference": {"complete_required_delivery_text": "Teen sleep — CDC general reference

For teenagers aged 13–17, CDC lists 8–10 hours of sleep daily as a general recommendation. Sleep quality also matters. Sleep difficulties or symptoms of a sleep disorder should be discussed with a healthcare provider. This reference is not an individualized basketball prescription or an adopted planning threshold.

Duration alone does not describe sleep quality.
Sleep problems and symptoms of a sleep disorder warrant healthcare-provider discussion.
Underlying citation: Paruthi S, Brooks LJ, D'Ambrosio C, et al. Recommended amount of sleep for pediatric populations: a consensus statement of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine. J Clin Sleep Med. 2016;12(6):785–786.
